claim: Google released Gemini 4 Neon for coding, reasoning and agent workflows.

support.quote: Today, we’re introducing Gemini 4 Neon — bringing frontier-level intelligence with fast end-to-end task completion across complex software engineering, knowledge work, and science workflows.

claim: Neon features a 1-million-token context window, four thinking levels, and $3/$15 per-million-token pricing positioned between Carbon and Hydrogen.

support.quote: The model is priced at $3 per million input tokens ($0.15 per million cached input tokens, a 95% discount) and $15 per million output tokens, with a 1 million-token context window.
While Carbon tackles your hardest, long-horizon projects and Hydrogen handles fast everyday execution, Neon balances depth and efficiency.
Gemini 4 Neon offers four effort levels (low, medium, high, and xhigh)

support.quote: Google DeepMind has released Gemini 4 Neon, its fourth model in just seven weeks.

claim: Neon supports a 1-million-token context window and four configurable thinking levels: low, medium, high, and xhigh.

claim: Google priced Gemini 4 Neon at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, with cached inputs discounted 95% to $0.15.

support.quote: The model is priced at $3 per million input tokens ($0.15 per million cached input tokens, a 95% discount) and $15 per million output tokens, with a 1 million-token context window.

claim: Neon pricing is 25% below Carbon standard pricing and 50% above Carbon promotional rates ending November 30, 2026.

support.quote: $3/$15 per 1M input/output tokens, 50% above Gemini 4 Carbon’s currently discounted price of $2/$10 (which ends on November 30), and 25% below its standard $4/$20.

claim: In Artificial Analysis testing, Neon averaged $6.44 and roughly 21 minutes per task, about 17% cheaper and 40% faster than Carbon, with output speed near 110 tokens per second.

support.quote: It costs $6.44 per task, ~17% less than Carbon ($7.76 at non-discounted pricing), and takes ~21 minutes per task, ~40% less than Carbon (~36 minutes).
and the lower time from its higher output speed (~110 vs ~57 output tokens per second)

claim: Neon uses roughly 15% more output tokens per task than Carbon, deriving cost savings from lower token prices.

support.quote: Neon uses ~15% more output tokens per task, so the lower cost comes purely from its 25% lower token prices

claim: In the Gemini app, Neon replaces Argon and Pro for $19.99 monthly Google AI Pro users, while Carbon remains exclusive to AI Ultra at $99.99 and free or AI Plus tiers receive no Neon.

support.quote: In Google AI Pro, the new model replaces Argon and the older Pro model, while Carbon stays exclusive to AI Ultra.
Google AI Pro costs $19.99 a month in the US and €21.99 in Germany.
Carbon, Google's most capable model, remains limited to AI Ultra, which starts at $99.99 a month.
Neon is not part of the free tier or Google AI Plus, which costs $4.99 a month.

claim: Neon scored 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, ranking third behind GPT-6.2 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2, and one point ahead of Carbon.

support.quote: Neon (xhigh) scores 61 on the Intelligence Index, 1 point ahead of Carbon (high), with small improvements in agentic knowledge work, visual reasoning and coding.
Neon (xhigh) scores 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, 1 point ahead of Gemini 4 Carbon (high) and 3rd overall, behind GPT-6.2 Astra (max) and Claude Fable 5.2 (max)

claim: Google reported Neon scored 58.6 on the Coding Agent Index, 65.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.1, and 39.0% on SWE-sweep inside Google Antigravity.

support.quote: ranking #1 overall on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index (58.6), with a score of 65.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.1
On SWE-sweep, it already leads on the mini-SWE harness (12.8%) and more than triples to a state-of-the-art 39.0% in Google Antigravity showing what the Antigravity harness unlocks.

claim: Artificial Analysis measured Neon scoring 59 on the Coding Agent Index in Antigravity CLI, three points ahead of Carbon.

support.quote: With Antigravity CLI, Neon (xhigh) scores 59 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, 3 points ahead of Carbon (high, 55).

claim: Neon averaged $6.86 per task in Antigravity, compared to $12.61 for Claude Opus 5.5 and $15.47 for Claude Fable 5.2.

support.quote: Gemini 4 Neon in Antigravity has an average Cost per Task of $6.86, compared to $12.61 for Claude Opus 5.5 (max) and $15.47 for Claude Fable 5.2 (xhigh).
